prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1187; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage does not match the story: the dents are on another side and at another height than the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Reported a left-turn collision at an intersection involving the insured vehicle and another vehicle. The claimant is represented by counsel, and the claim is open for a bodily injury component.

Entry 2: Spoke with the insured, who confirmed the vehicle was turning left when another car struck it. The insured is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle and records the same basic sequence of events. Two independent witnesses gave statements consistent with the reported collision.

Entry 4: Reviewed scene photographs and the other driver's statement, both of which support that the collision occurred as described. No prior damage to the insured vehicle appears in our file or in the records we pulled.

Entry 5: The claimant's shoulder injury is consistent with the type and force of a side impact of this kind. No prior complaints involving that body area are on record.

Entry 6: The damage on the vehicle is located on a different side and at a different height than the impact described in the account, and the appraiser has flagged this for further review. Requested the appraiser's measurements and the repair estimate for comparison.

Entry 7: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this type of injury, and the medical records are being requested from the treating providers. The claimant has given the same account of events in every conversation so far.

Entry 8: Referred the file for a secondary review of the damage pattern against the reported impact, and will coordinate all further contact through counsel. No coverage question has been identified at this stage.
